name: painted ground
description: An example made for the landing page, not a library game. Five knights a side on a seven-by-seven board, and every square a knight lands on is painted its owner's colour; the first to hold 25 of the 49 squares wins, and taking every enemy knight wins too. Any square can be painted back, and that is the flaw it exists to show: landing on the other side's square swings the count by two, landing on an empty one by only one, so both players stop claiming empty ground, the count stalls a few squares short and the game runs out of moves.

provenance.history: Constructed by LPR2 as the landing page's ground story (docs/archive/plan-landing.md section 2.1), the user allowing a constructed example where the library's pair was unclear. It differs from ground-for-good.json only in rules.territory.mode. Not a library game, not measured; its boards on the page are games played through Engine by make_examples.py. Moved from docs/reference/landing-mockups/examples/ to chess_variant_sandbox/web/stories/ by LP1 (2026-10-24), its mechanics unchanged.
